subject: Badgeless walk-up capture + WiFi portal fallback for HubSpot ingest
messages:
From: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@eventco.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: wifiops@eventco.com
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: lead capture ask: badgeless walk-ups + wifi fallback

Hey Rafael —

Quick intro: I run operations for EventCo and we need a simple plan for lead capture when badge scanners fail or when attendees come as walk-ups without printed badges. Our on-site vendor (Mark at Expo Network) proposed a captive WiFi portal that prompts for name, email, company and opt-in. We want those records to flow into HubSpot in near-real-time and include an explicit consent record that we can surface later.

Main constraints:
- Limited badge scanners (10% of stations down last year).
- Spawned leads must dedupe against badge-scanned attendees.
- Privacy requires a timestamped consent flag and the exact text shown to the user.
- WiFi vendor can add a redirect to a URL or write to a webhook.

Can Redwood accept a webhook from the wifi portal and route it to HubSpot with dedupe logic + consent capture? If yes, what fields do you need, and any sample consent language we should use? I've attached a quick wireframe of the portal.

Attachments: wifi-portal-wireframe.png

Appreciate a quick feasibility note and a rough rollout plan. We go live at SummitWest on 2026-06-10.

Thanks,
Sarah Cole
Head of Operations, EventCo

---
This message may contain information intended for Redwood and EventCo coordination.
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@eventco.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: lead capture ask: badgeless walk-ups + wifi fallback

Thanks Sarah — short answer: yes, we can. Looping in Ben (integrations) and Laura (field ops) to scope the mapping, consent, and rollout.

High-level approach:
1) WiFi portal posts a JSON payload to a Redwood endpoint (or a vendor webhook we proxy).
2) Redwood validates and normalizes fields, writes an event to our ingest queue.
3) We apply dedupe heuristics (email primary, fallback to name+company+phone), attach a consent object (text + timestamp + source=wifi_portal).
4) For HubSpot we can either:
   - Push directly to HubSpot Forms API (for automatic contact create + form submission), OR
   - Batch forward to a HubSpot ingestion endpoint (private account-level API) if you prefer server-to-server.

Questions for EventCo / Expo Network:
- Will the portal capture phone? (helps dedupe)
- Does the vendor support a server webhook vs only redirect-to-form?
- Any existing HubSpot portal/form IDs you want us to post into?

Consent text (suggested short):
By signing in to the event Wi‑Fi you agree to receive communications from EventCo about this event and relevant product updates. You can unsubscribe at any time.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben: can you draft required payload schema and minimal field set?
- Laura: propose a 2-stage on-site test (canary + ramp) and a tape-out checklist for scanners vs wifi fallback.

We can do a short discovery call with Sarah + Mark this week. Sarah — are you available Thu 4/23 10am PT?

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Partner Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks Rafael — adding technical detail.

Minimal payload we need from the wifi portal (JSON POST):
- event_id (string)
- source: "wifi_portal"
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- name
- email
- company (optional)
- phone (optional)
- consent_text (string) // exact copy shown to user
- consent_given (boolean)
- client_ip (optional)
- redirect_id (optional) // for analytics matchback

Dedupe policy (configurable):
1) If email present -> match contact by email in HubSpot and attach the submission as a new form submission metadata entry.
2) Else: fuzzy-match by name+company+phone. We store a match_score; if score < threshold, create a new contact with a high-confidence tag that it originated from wifi fallback.

HubSpot integration options:
- Forms API: submit to a dedicated hidden form. Pros: visible in HubSpot activity, simple. Cons: limited server-to-server enrichments.
- Contacts API + Engagements: create/update contact then create a custom engagement with consent payload. Pros: richer audit trail (we can push consent_text into engagement body). Requires OAuth for EventCo.

Rate limits: expect bursts during key sessions; recommend provisioning for 300 rps across all portals or implement local batch buffering (we can accept batches of up to 1k events every 30s).

I've attached a starting CSV mapping for your HubSpot fields and a sample webhook curl.

Attachments: hubspot-field-mapping.csv

Let me know if the vendor supports webhook auth (HMAC) or only simple POSTs. If no HMAC, we recommend a short-lived signed redirect (we can host a small proxy).

- Ben
Ben Carter
Integrations Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sarah / team —

Operational notes and rollout timeline from field ops perspective:

On-site test plan (recommended):
- Day -7: Integration smoke test with a single portal pointing at Redwood staging endpoint. Validate payload, HMAC signature (if used), and HubSpot ingest flow.
- Day -3: Canary run on one entrance during off-peak hours (10AM-12PM). Gate scanners remain primary — wifi portal is flagged with a low-confidence tag.
- Day 0 (go-live): Enable portal at all entrances + session-level sampling for verification. Continue to run dedupe job hourly for first 48 hours.

Acceptance criteria:
- <1% false duplicates (contacts merged erroneously) in the first 24h.
- Consent text stored and visible on contact timeline as an engagement.
- Failover behavior: if HubSpot is rate-limited, events persist in our queue and retry with exponential backoff up to 24 hours.

Privacy/consent suggestion: use Ben's short text but add a link to full privacy details. Example full line for the portal: 
"By signing in to EventCo Wi‑Fi you agree to receive communications from EventCo about this event and related products. View our privacy policy: https://eventco.com/privacy. You can unsubscribe at any time."

Operational items for EventCo to confirm:
- Provide HubSpot OAuth client or an API key with ingestion scope for the account/form we should target.
- Confirm whether you want 'source' to be recorded as 'wifi_portal' or 'onsite_fallback' for analytics.
- Confirm if phone should be required (we recommend optional).

I'll drive the on-site test checklist and coordinate with Expo Network for the staging webhook. Olga — can your team run the live ingestion sampling and deliver the weekly report?

Laura Bennett
Senior Field Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
